system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty cap of **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Higher cap, or at least a separate cap reflecting identifiable risks and excluding fundamental, tax, IP, fraud and indemnity claims. | **Reject as drafted** — the cap is too restrictive for a AUD 24m acquisition and known exposures already exceed ordinary warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket; only excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis; deductible basket or lower tipping threshold; aggregation of related claims. | **Seek deductible basket and lower thresholds** — the proposal could leave substantial leakage unrecovered. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Claims notified within 18 months; potentially applies to all Claims. | 24–36 months for general warranties, with longer periods for tax, employment, privacy, IP and known matters. | **Extend and differentiate periods** — statutory, tax, privacy and IP issues may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general cap and time limits. | Uncapped or substantially higher cap; survival for the limitation period and preferably indefinitely for title/capacity. | **Reject** — title to 100% of the shares is core consideration, not ordinary warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out; limitations apply to all Claims. | No limitation, exclusion, non-reliance protection or exclusive-remedy provision for fraud, wilful misconduct or fraudulent concealment. | **Insist on express carve-out** — a seller must not contract out of liability for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Fair disclosure against each warranty, with sufficient detail, no deemed disclosure from the entire data room or public searches. | **Reject blanket disclosure** — it defeats the warranty package and makes liability unpredictable. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known or discoverable by Buyer or advisers, including from the data room/public records. | Actual knowledge of specified senior Buyer personnel only; no “constructive” or adviser knowledge; no waiver of warranty claims. | **Limit to actual knowledge** — “discoverable” knowledge improperly shifts diligence and interpretation risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent currently disclosed. | Consent and satisfaction of all conditions as a completion condition, or termination/price protection if unavailable; specific indemnity for loss. | **Make a condition precedent** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and consent risk is material. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility and security to be released after Completion. | Repayment, release and discharge of all security at or before Completion, evidenced by enforceable payoff/release documents; no residual debt. | **Reject post-Completion release** — it conflicts with debt-free/cash-free delivery and exposes Buyer to creditor/security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, super and on-costs unclear. | Seller-funded settlement before/at Completion, including all taxes and on-costs, with price adjustment or retention/escrow. | **Require dollar-for-dollar adjustment and indemnity** — these are transaction-related liabilities that would otherwise remain with the Company. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, apparently AUD 180,000, and considered adequate. | Indemnity covering all costs and losses from failure to obtain the Project Materials/IP, including replacement, infringement, remediation and consequential transaction costs. | **Expand and preserve the indemnity** — payment of one fee does not establish transfer or protect the Company’s ability to use the IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident; scope, access and notification obligations unknown; no admitted breach or loss. | Specific indemnity, full investigation and remediation covenant, regulatory/customer notification cooperation, and no reliance on materiality; consider escrow/retention. | **Treat as a known special risk** — personal data may have been exposed and regulatory obligations can crystallise after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three related renewals totalling AUD 330,000 characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Details of term, termination, accrual and necessity; completion-date adjustment for pre-Completion commitments or a specific indemnity. | **Do not accept the characterisation** — the contracts may create material post-Completion liabilities not reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Broad limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; fundamental claims use general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, fraud, known matters and specific indemnities, with tailored caps and survival periods. | **Insist on category separation** — materially different risks cannot sensibly share one cap, basket and limitation period. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%. | Signed title warranty covering legal and beneficial ownership, 100% issued shares, no encumbrances/options/trusts, valid issue and transfer authority, backed by registry evidence and undertakings. | **Require independent verification and enhanced warranty** — a share register alone may not establish unencumbered beneficial title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP positions are settled under the general warranty regime. | Specific tax covenant/indemnity and robust IP warranties/indemnity, including ownership, chain of title, infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments and data rights. | **Keep open and separate** — tax and IP liabilities can be large, latent and poorly protected by general warranties. |

**Overall:** the draft attempts to convert known and potentially material risks into general disclosure and a low, short-lived liability package. The Buyer should make Completion conditional on Bluefen and Riverlark resolution, obtain specific protection for the known matters, and reject blanket disclosure, constructive knowledge and cross-category limitations.
=== END ADVICE ===
